  Threat: Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen, Alert at Home: I feel on guard even inside my own home, Scanning for Danger: I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
  Memory: Cannot Find Words: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it, Feels Present Not Past: The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over, Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
  Negative Appraisals: Distrust Others: People are not what they seem, Identity Loss: I feel like I don't know myself anymore, Body Unreliable: I can no longer trust my own body

Vignette:
Ravi, a 58-year-old fisherman of South Asian descent, had spent his entire life navigating the ever-changing tides of the sea. For years, he found solace in the rhythm of the waves and the thrill of casting his nets into the vast blue. However, everything changed one fateful afternoon two years ago when a sudden storm transformed his familiar world into a scene of chaos and terror. As he struggled to secure his boat against the furious winds and crashing waves, a rogue wave struck, capsizing his vessel and sending him into the icy depths of the ocean. In that harrowing moment, the water felt like a suffocating shroud, and he was convinced he would not survive. Miraculously, he did, but the scars left by that life-threatening accident would haunt him far longer than the physical ones.

In the months that followed, Ravi's life became a shadow of its former self. Initially, he tried to resume his daily routine, but the once-comforting solitude of the sea now felt menacing. The simplest sounds of the world around him—the rustle of leaves, the call of distant gulls—turned into reminders of the storm and the chaos that had ensued. He found himself especially unsettled during interactions with strangers. Conversations that would once have felt casual and welcoming now left him feeling exposed and vulnerable. Whenever he had to talk to someone he didn’t know, anxiety gripped him; he felt as though their intentions were hidden, that they might represent an unpredictable threat, just like the wave that had changed everything.

Ravi's heightened sense of threat permeated his home life as well. He had come to believe that silence, which once provided a tranquil backdrop to his evenings, now signaled impending danger. The quietness felt ominous, laced with the tension of unspoken fears. Even within the four walls of his small home, he felt perpetually on guard, scanning the corners of his living room and peering out of the window as if danger might emerge from the shadows. This vigilance seeped into his everyday life, making it difficult for him to relax, and his nights became filled with restless tossing and turning.

The memories of the accident were a different kind of torment. Ravi knew precisely what happened that day, but when he tried to articulate it, the words escaped him, as if they were submerged beneath the surface of his consciousness. Instead, the memory would erupt unbidden, as vivid and terrifying as it had been on that stormy afternoon. The terror returned with a ferocity that left him breathless, making him feel as though he were still fighting for his life in the cold embrace of the ocean. It was as if the past was not so distant after all; every recollection felt immediate and alive, jarring him back into that moment of fear.

As time wore on, Ravi began to grapple with a profound sense of identity loss. The man he once knew—a confident fisherman, capable and self-sufficient—seemed to fade further away with each passing day. The accident had left him feeling unmoored, as if his sense of self had been swept away by the very tides he had once mastered. He distrusted others, feeling that they concealed their true selves beneath facades. This distrust extended even to himself; his body felt foreign and unreliable, a vessel that had betrayed him at the moment he needed it most. With every wave of anxiety that washed over him, he succumbed to the belief that he could no longer trust his own instincts.

The culmination of these experiences eventually propelled Ravi to seek help. After months of isolation and emotional turmoil, he found himself in the waiting room of a clinic, heart racing and palms sweaty. What frightened him most was the thought of exposing his vulnerabilities, of admitting that he could not navigate this storm alone. Yet, deep down, he clung to a fragile hope: perhaps with the right support, he could begin to reclaim his identity and find a way to trust both himself and the world around him once again.
